evidence.CORE-002: src/core/engine/lifecycle.test.ts::a full play cycle follows the declared transitions (SYS-LIFECYCLE-01) — asserts deal → night → day → night, so play starts with night and each night/day is followed by the other.
evidence.DAY-002: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::a living player may nominate only once per day and a player may be nominated only once per day (SYS-VOTES-01) — a second nomination by the same player returns error.10 and nominating an already nominated player returns error.14.
evidence.DAY-003: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::a living player may nominate only once per day and a player may be nominated only once per day (SYS-VOTES-01) — after kill(state, "4"), nominate(state, "4", "5") returns error.11, so a dead player cannot nominate.
evidence.INFO-001: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::every Trouble Brewing first-night information role offers allowed false information while impaired (SYS-EFFECTS-01, TB-EMPATH-03) — each impaired information role is offered allowed false answers, so the Storyteller may give false information when the ability fails.
evidence.SETUP-006: src/core/engine/setup.test.ts::each setup modifier shifts the composition like its official source — for Baron, Godfather, Fang Gu and Vigormortis the shift keeps the total equal to the player count.
evidence.SETUP-014: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::5–6 player first night has no evil introduction and no bluffs (SYS-SETUP-04) — a five-player night has no minioninfo or demoninfo step while a seven-player night has both.
evidence.STATUS-004: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::every Trouble Brewing first-night information role offers allowed false information while impaired (SYS-EFFECTS-01, TB-EMPATH-03) — an impaired information role's answer is a host choice among allowed false options.
evidence.VOTE-005: src/core/engine/engine.test.ts::dead votes count once, are spent on a failed nomination, and cannot repeat (SYS-VOTES-03) — the dead voter's token becomes false and a later nomination counts zero for them.
evidence.ROLE-ARTIST-001: src/core/engine/snv.test.ts::the Artist records one private yes/no question and spends the ability (SNV-ARTIST-01) — during the day one non-empty question is stored privately and a second is rejected.
evidence.ROLE-ARTIST-006: src/core/engine/snv.test.ts::the Artist records one private yes/no question and spends the ability (SNV-ARTIST-01) — used.artist becomes true and a second question is rejected, so the ability is spent after the question.
evidence.ROLE-CERENOVUS-001: src/core/engine/snv.test.ts::the Cerenovus has a step on every night, choosing one player and a good character (SNV-CERENOVUS-01) — the step record on nights 1 and 2 has minTargets/maxTargets 1 and roleChoices limited to the good roles.
evidence.ROLE-DREAMER-003: src/core/engine/snv.test.ts::a sober Dreamer offers only the target's character with an opposite-kind character (SNV-DREAMER-01) — every option is a good/evil pair with exactly one true character.
evidence.ROLE-DREAMER-006: src/core/engine/snv.test.ts::an impaired Dreamer may show any good and evil pair, a Vortox forbids the true one (SNV-DREAMER-01) — under a Vortox no option contains the true character and submitting the true pair is refused.
evidence.ROLE-MUTANT-001: src/core/engine/snv.test.ts::the Mutant is mad about being an Outsider while in play (SNV-MUTANT-01) — the Mutant madness token exists and the Storyteller's execute penalty kills the Mutant.
evidence.ROLE-MUTANT-002: src/core/engine/snv.test.ts::a Mutant can be executed on the first night (Mutant r1755) — the madness execute penalty is allowed during night 1, outside the nomination phase.
evidence.ROLE-ORACLE-002: src/core/engine/snv.test.ts::the Oracle counts dead evil players, not death events (SNV-ORACLE-01) — the count is of currently dead evil players, and a resurrected player drops out of it.
evidence.ROLE-ORACLE-005: src/core/engine/snv.test.ts::a living Vortox forbids the true Oracle count (SNV-ORACLE-01) — the true count is not among the options and the step requires a false answer.
evidence.ROLE-SAGE-003: src/core/engine/snv.test.ts::a Pit-Hag-created Demon does not take the Demon turn and its deaths are not Demon attacks (SNV-PITHAG-01) — a Pit-Hag death is not a Demon attack and the Sage does not wake for it.
evidence.ROLE-SAVANT-002: src/core/engine/snv.test.ts::the Savant information stays one true and one false unless impaired (SNV-SAVANT-02) — a healthy Savant's "both true" answer is rejected, so the two statements must be one true and one false.
evidence.ROLE-SAVANT-006: src/core/engine/snv.test.ts::a living Vortox makes both Savant statements false (SNV-SAVANT-03) — a true statement is rejected and only the "neither" answer is allowed.

gaps.CORE-001: No test asserts the per-player character/alignment pair or its secrecy; setup tests assert bag composition and a deal permutation only.
gaps.CORE-003: No test asserts daytime discussion; voting is covered by SYS-VOTES, so the sentence is not mechanically verified.
gaps.CORE-004: SYS-NIGHT-01's test asserts the official night-order data, not that those characters wake and act; no single test asserts the sentence's wake behavior.
gaps.CORE-005: Players may speak freely at any time; this is player conduct with no engine behavior or test.
gaps.CORE-006: Not showing a token or reading the Grimoire is player conduct; no engine test.
gaps.CORE-007: Storyteller neutrality and rules help are outside engine behavior.
gaps.CORE-008: Player etiquette is not engine behavior.
gaps.CORE-009: Discussion by dead players is not modeled; dead-team outcomes are asserted only inside role rules (Evil Twin, Klutz), not for this general sentence.
gaps.CORE-010: Dead voting is covered by SYS-VOTES-03, but the sentence also claims dead players keep talking, which no test asserts.
gaps.CORE-011: The 'choose' wording rule (player decides, otherwise the Storyteller) is not asserted anywhere; the app records host choices uniformly.
gaps.CORE-012: The 'might' wording rule (Storyteller decides whether it happens) is not asserted by a test.
gaps.DAY-001: Lifecycle tests assert the night/day alternation, but daytime discussion has no test and SYS-VOTES-01 covers nomination limits only.
gaps.DEATH-001: No test asserts the alive/dead dichotomy as a state rule.
gaps.DEATH-002: An attack on a dead player is asserted only for the Fang Gu (SNV-FANGGU-03); the general rule and the 'group does not learn' clause have no engine test.
gaps.DEATH-003: Death ending persistent effects is asserted only inside role rules (Vigormortis, No Dashii, Cerenovus); no shared rule test asserts the general sentence.
gaps.DEATH-004: No test asserts the sources of death as a general statement.
gaps.EXEC-001: No test asserts the definition of an execution (group decision, non-Traveller, daytime); the Traveller exclusion is unmodeled.
gaps.EXEC-002: No single test asserts both halves: the only-execution rule is refused by 'official execution of a dead player records an event without another death', while an execution-free day is asserted elsewhere.
gaps.EXEC-003: No test asserts the surviving-via-ability case as the day's execution: the Sailor test asserts survival with no death, and the execution-event test uses an already dead player.
gaps.EXEC-004: Exile is not modeled; no test.
gaps.EXEC-005: Exile is not modeled; no test.
gaps.EXEC-006: Exile is not modeled; no test.
gaps.EXEC-007: No test executes a player on more than one day; the dead-player execution tests assert a single event without a death.
gaps.INFO-002: Truthful answers to rules questions for impaired players are not engine behavior and have no test.
gaps.INFO-003: No single test covers dead and impaired together; SYS-EFFECTS-01 asserts impaired information as a host answer and SYS-NIGHT-03 asserts one killed actor is skipped.
gaps.INFO-004: SYS-SETUP-04 asserts that the demoninfo step exists at seven or more players, not that the Demon learns the Minions or receives three good off-script bluffs.
gaps.INFO-005: SYS-SETUP-04 asserts that the minioninfo step exists at seven or more players, not what the Minions learn.
gaps.INFO-006: The mid-game clause is asserted by the Pit-Hag test and the first-night clause only per role; no single test asserts the definition.
gaps.INFO-007: Regaining a used once-per-game ability is asserted only for the Assassin (BMR-ASSASSIN-02); the resurrected first-night clause has no rule-level test.
gaps.NIGHT-001: No single test asserts who wakes and that players close their eyes; SYS-NIGHT-01 asserts order and SYS-NIGHT-03 asserts one skipped dead actor.
gaps.NIGHT-002: Physical wake gestures are not engine behavior.
gaps.NIGHT-003: Storyteller gestures are not engine behavior.
gaps.NIGHT-004: The dawn announcement's content is not asserted; no test covers what the group learns.
gaps.NIGHT-005: When players may discuss their characters is not engine behavior.
gaps.NIGHT-006: 'Each night*' is a glossary term; tests assert per-role step schedules, not the term's meaning.
gaps.ROLE-ARTIST-002: No test asserts the answer wording (Yes/No/I don't know); the answer is host input.
gaps.ROLE-ARTIST-003: The test asserts only that the question text is absent from the public view; it does not assert that the answer or the whole conversation stays private.
gaps.ROLE-ARTIST-004: No test asserts initiative; the command only requires the character holder.
gaps.ROLE-ARTIST-005: Asking the player to rephrase is not engine behavior and is untested.
gaps.ROLE-BARBER-002: Alignment preservation is asserted, but 'each learns their new character' is not; the swap test asserts roles only.
gaps.ROLE-BARBER-004: The test asserts only the start-knowing handover; it does not assert that a once-per-game ability is fresh for the new holder.
gaps.ROLE-CERENOVUS-002: No test asserts that the chosen player learns of the madness; the engine stores the token for the host.
gaps.ROLE-CERENOVUS-003: The day execution and the night execution are asserted by different tests; no single test covers both.
gaps.ROLE-CERENOVUS-004: Whether a hint is a noticeable effort is Storyteller discretion; no test.
gaps.ROLE-CERENOVUS-005: Whether a mad evil player is executed is Storyteller discretion; no test.
gaps.ROLE-CERENOVUS-006: The test records the madness execution on the day; it does not assert that it is the day's only execution.
gaps.ROLE-CERENOVUS-007: The penalty test asserts the Storyteller chooses, but 'the player is never obliged to be mad' is player conduct no test asserts.
gaps.ROLE-CLOCKMAKER-004: Travellers are not modeled; no test asserts that evil Travellers are excluded from the Minion count.
gaps.ROLE-DREAMER-001: Self-exclusion is tested, but Traveller exclusion is not modelable and untested.
gaps.ROLE-DREAMER-002: Self-exclusion is tested, but Traveller exclusion is untested.
gaps.ROLE-DREAMER-004: Only a Townsfolk target is tested; the Minion/Demon target branch is not asserted.
gaps.ROLE-DREAMER-005: No test asserts that the player cannot tell which of the two characters is true.
gaps.ROLE-FLOWERGIRL-003: Exile is not modeled; no test.
gaps.ROLE-FLOWERGIRL-005: No test asserts that several Demons, including dead ones, each make the answer yes.
gaps.ROLE-FLOWERGIRL-006: The DID YOU VOTE TODAY Storyteller procedure is not engine behavior.
gaps.ROLE-JUGGLER-002: No test asserts that the guesses are public.
gaps.ROLE-JUGGLER-005: The impairment test poisons the Juggler at night, not on the guessing day.
gaps.ROLE-JUGGLER-006: No test asserts that a Juggler who dies before the night gets no information.
gaps.ROLE-KLUTZ-001: The public-choice test asserts the choice and its timing; the living-target requirement is asserted in a different test and the public declaration of being the Klutz is not asserted.
gaps.ROLE-KLUTZ-002: Player deliberation and advice are not engine behavior.
gaps.ROLE-KLUTZ-006: Cheating by avoiding the choice is outside engine behavior.
gaps.ROLE-MATHEMATICIAN-004: No single test covers both clauses: one asserts the Mathematician cannot record its own ability, another asserts it counts other abnormal abilities.
gaps.ROLE-MATHEMATICIAN-006: The specific anomaly examples (Recluse as evil to the Chef, poisoned Soldier death, poisoned Empath true information) are not asserted.
gaps.ROLE-MUTANT-003: No test asserts that a daytime madness execution ends the day and blocks a second execution.
gaps.ROLE-MUTANT-004: No test covers a night hint after the day already had an execution, or the next day remaining available.
gaps.ROLE-MUTANT-005: The review test asserts the Storyteller may record no penalty; 'the player is never obliged to be mad' is player conduct no test asserts.
gaps.ROLE-MUTANT-006: The Storyteller's judgment of effort is not asserted.
gaps.ROLE-NO-DASHII-003: The nearest-Townsfolk test asserts one dead Townsfolk target; 'always two Townsfolk' is not asserted.
gaps.ROLE-NO-DASHII-005: The reconciliation test asserts a source ceasing to be the No Dashii and a target changing character; a new player becoming the No Dashii is not asserted.
gaps.ROLE-ORACLE-004: No test counts a dead player whose alignment differs from the printed one (a flipped token).
gaps.ROLE-PHILOSOPHER-004: No test covers a chosen character that was absent at the choice and appears later.
gaps.ROLE-PHILOSOPHER-006: A fresh once-per-game ability is asserted on regaining the Philosopher, but choosing a new or the same ability is not.
gaps.ROLE-PIT-HAG-004: The test asserts that the Storyteller marks arbitrary deaths after a Demon is created; it does not assert the 'or protect' choice, and no single test covers the full decision.
gaps.ROLE-PIT-HAG-007: Recommendations for handling the created Demon are advice, not an engine rule, and have no test.
gaps.ROLE-SAGE-004: No test asserts the usual living/living pair or the final-night living/dead pair.
gaps.ROLE-SAVANT-001: The test asserts a private visit once per day; it does not assert that the Savant may decline to visit.
gaps.ROLE-SAVANT-003: No test asserts that the player cannot tell which statement is true.
gaps.ROLE-SAVANT-004: The test asserts that the statements are absent from the public view; it does not assert that the whole conversation, including the answer, stays private.
gaps.ROLE-SAVANT-005: The test asserts an impaired Savant may receive two true statements; two false statements are not asserted.
gaps.ROLE-SAVANT-007: Usefulness and game relevance, and not naming the Demon, are advice; no test.
gaps.ROLE-SEAMSTRESS-004: No test selects a dead player or a Traveller; only living targets are exercised.
gaps.ROLE-SEAMSTRESS-005: No test asserts that the Storyteller may decline the ability for a night.
gaps.ROLE-SWEETHEART-004: The test asserts that the chosen player becomes drunk, not that any team may be chosen.
gaps.ROLE-VIGORMORTIS-006: The test asserts the neighbour poison ends when the killed Minion stops being a Minion; it does not assert that the dead Minion loses its retained ability.
gaps.ROLE-VORTOX-003: No test asserts that non-ability information (rules explanations, character or alignment changes) is unaffected by the Vortox.
gaps.ROLE-VORTOX-005: Exile is not modeled; no test.
gaps.ROLE-WITCH-003: No test asserts the one-day curse duration or that the same player may be cursed again.
gaps.SETUP-001: The script parser rejects fewer than five players, but the 'at least seven recommended' clause is advice and untested.
gaps.SETUP-002: The mixed-pool test asserts a custom script is rejected without manual-only mode; it does not assert that a game chooses exactly one of the three official editions.
gaps.SETUP-003: The composition test asserts the number of characters per player count, not that the Storyteller chooses them secretly.
gaps.SETUP-004: No test asserts that tokens are ordered in the Grimoire by seating order; only role-by-seat assignment is validated.
gaps.SETUP-005: The composition test asserts the bracket shift; no test asserts that it applies only at setup and is not repeated during play.
gaps.SETUP-008: The random-bag, deal-permutation and public-projection tests are separate; no single test asserts the secret draw and that a player does not show the token.
gaps.SETUP-009: Traveller overflow above fifteen players is not supported or tested.
gaps.SETUP-010: The first-game recommendation about Travellers and Fabled is advice, not engine behavior.
gaps.SETUP-011: Physical seating arrangement is not engine behavior.
gaps.SETUP-012: Physical Grimoire placement is not engine behavior.
gaps.SETUP-013: The Town Square components are not modeled or tested.
gaps.ST-001: Storyteller duties are not engine behavior.
gaps.ST-002: The Storyteller's permission to lie in play is not asserted by a test.
gaps.ST-003: Public consequence-without-cause wording is not asserted.
gaps.ST-004: Pretending an impaired ability works is not asserted as a general rule.
gaps.ST-005: The 'choose' wording rule is not asserted.
gaps.ST-006: The 'might' wording rule is not asserted.
gaps.STATUS-001: The paired-state dichotomy is not asserted as a rule; partial state checks exist inside role tests.
gaps.STATUS-002: Tests cover drunk or poisoned impairment of specific roles and registrations; no shared test asserts that the two give the same no-ability effect.
gaps.STATUS-003: Hiding impairment from the player is not asserted; effects are exposed to the host only.
gaps.STATUS-005: A once-per-game ability spent while impaired is asserted only inside role rules (Slayer, Professor, Courtier); no shared test.
gaps.STATUS-006: An ability returning when sober or healthy is asserted per role (Cerenovus, Witch, Pukka); no shared test.
gaps.STATUS-007: No test asserts that drunk and poisoned can coexist without cancelling.
gaps.STATUS-008: No test asserts as a general rule that abilities applied to an impaired player work normally.
gaps.STATUS-009: No test asserts as a general rule that impairment stays on the player across a character change.
gaps.STATUS-010: Alignment/character independence is asserted only inside specific swaps; no shared test.
gaps.STATUS-011: Secret notification of an alignment or character change is not asserted.
gaps.STATUS-012: The general meaning of registration is not asserted; only Spy/Recluse registration behavior is.
gaps.STATUS-013: Madness is implemented per role; no shared test asserts the general definition or that players are never obliged.
gaps.STATUS-014: The Storyteller's final judgment of madness is not asserted as a general rule.
gaps.STATUS-015: Revealing former madness without a penalty has no engine behavior or test.
gaps.STATUS-016: Alive-neighbour computation is asserted per role (Empath, Tea Lady); no shared rule or test asserts both glossary definitions.
gaps.VOTE-001: The dead one-vote rule is covered by SYS-VOTES-03, but the sentence also claims unlimited living votes, which no cited test asserts.
gaps.VOTE-002: Clockwise vote order is not asserted; recordVotes takes an explicit player set.
gaps.VOTE-003: SYS-VOTES-02 asserts only the half threshold; the 'more votes than any other nominee' clause has no rule and no cited test.
gaps.VOTE-004: A test asserts that ties block execution, but no engine rule cites it and SYS-VOTES-02 asserts only the threshold.
gaps.WIN-002: The two-alive evil win is exercised only from an Imp attack test (TB-IMP-01); SYS-WINS-02's tests assert win priority, not this general condition, and the Traveller exclusion is unmodeled.
gaps.WIN-003: The Evil Twin test asserts a dead player's team wins; no test asserts the 'lose as one team' half as a general rule.
gaps.WIN-004: Role team assignment is used by setup counts, but no test asserts the alignment rule itself.
